section_anchor: The part of the Class80 worth remembering
brief_summary: Three-column comparison card contrasting the Class80's three selectable mount builds — top mount (plate bolted to the case, firm/no-give feel), PCB gasket mount with plate (plate floats on gasket pads, soft/uniform feel, highlighted in bronze as the gasket-mount signature), and plateless PCB gasket (no plate, PCB on gasket pads alone, loose/bouncy feel) — all sold under the same nameplate.
data_sources: data/boards/class80.json description — 'a choice of top mount, PCB gasket mount with plate, or plateless PCB gasket'

mounting-styles-compared.mdx § 'Gasket-mount' — 'The CLASS80 from MM Studio takes the same approach in a TKL chassis — CNC aluminum with both top-mount and gasket-mount configurations available from a single board — and is one of the more studied examples of how a multi-mode mount system changes the shape of the builder's decision.'
mounting-styles-compared.mdx § 'Top-mount' — 'The feel is firmer and more direct. There is essentially no give.'
mounting-styles-compared.mdx § 'Gasket-mount' — 'Gasket boards read as deeper, rounder, and more uniform across the board than any of the other three styles.'

mounting-styles-compared.mdx § 'Tray-mount and the no plate fixing family' — 'The result is a looser, bouncier feel than tray-mount with a fixed plate... Builders who like the sensation describe it as marshmallow.'
